title: Beats travel-specific apps for travel planning
body:
I was planning a 10-day motorcycle trip and tried so many different apps to organize everything and use as a hub for hotel info, sight-seeing locations, time management, maps, file attachments for tickets and national park maps, etc…but every app was a major flop. 

A quick monthly sub to unlock the map view made Trello the nearly perfect tool I was looking for. The only thing missing was auto-calculating time between map locations, but I was able to manually do it and use a few customized and color-coded tags to put that info on each card to see at a glance.

Everything else was perfect: being able to use my board offline in remote areas, being able to share the board with my husband so he had access to all the info, attachments, map layout, adding dates to harness the schedule view, adding comments to track ideas, hyperlinks to web content and navigation routes, notes for check-in info at hotels and timed park entry, even being able to check off the things we got to see and what we didn’t have time for. Trello did all of this SO MUCH BETTER than tailor-made travel apps like Wanderlog.

Trello is just so versatile. Obviously great for trip planning, but also project tracking for freelance work, and creative hobbies like sewing projects. One of the best apps out there.

title: Great... If You Enjoy Being Locked Out of Your Own Business
body:
To be honest, Trello used to be a great productivity tool — until Atlassian showed up with their magic trick: locking paying users out of their accounts with surprise 2FA prompts nobody ever set up. Brilliant.

Imagine running a business, managing projects, staying on top of deliverables… and then suddenly you can’t log in on desktop because Trello decided you should have 2FA credentials that you never received. No recovery codes. No setup flow. No warning. Just *poof* — productivity gone.

The cherry on top? You can’t even contact support because you need to log in to do that — which you obviously can’t, because, well, 2FA. I'm two days behind on major work, stuck on a mobile app UI that feels like it was designed as an afterthought, and completely locked out of critical project boards on desktop.

This isn’t a bug — this is a UX disaster dressed as a “security feature.” And while Trello’s parent company Atlassian might think they’re tightening security, they’re really just tightening the noose around their own product’s credibility.

For a platform built on the promise of helping businesses stay organized, this rollout was anything but. If you’re running a serious business, look elsewhere — until Trello figures out how to secure accounts *without* locking out their users in the process.
developer_response:
Hi there! We're sorry to hear about the issues you've been experiencing so far. Most likely, the verification code you're receiving isn't related to 2FA, but rather with our OTP code verification we have enabled for all Atlassian accounts that don't have a two-step verification enabled on their accounts. This is to ensure and protect our customers' accounts from unauthorized access and to prevent malicious actors from gaining access to your Atlassian account if your email address gets compromised. 

You can find more about this change here: https://www.atlassian.com/blog/announcements/atlassian-account-protection-enhancements 

If you have more questions, please reach out to us by contacting us through our contact form at https://support.atlassian.com/contact/. We'll be happy to help you clarify it.

And God bless the developers, because the free version is incredibly useful and helps people at many levels, from students to dreamers, keep everything organized!

I would like to suggest an enhancement for the "due date" feature. While the cards are currently organized by due date, it would be extremely beneficial if they could also sort by specific times. When multiple cards share the same due date but have different times, it can lead to confusion. Having the ability to view and organize these cards by both date and time would greatly improve clarity and efficiency.

I've also noticed that recently, when I open the app on my phone, the cards do not appear in the same lists as they do on my computer. Ensuring that the lists are synchronized across devices would greatly enhance the user experience. 

Thanks for looking into this Trello Team! However 5 starts for the app!
